title: prisoner
description: A prisoner embodies the paradox of presence within absence, holding consciousness in spaces designed for containment rather than expansion, where time becomes both the medium and the message of existence. This role manifests through the navigation of imposed stillness, the preservation of interior life against erasure, and the translation of constraint into various forms of witness—whether through memory, adaptation, or the quiet resistance of maintaining humanity within systems designed to diminish it. The prisoner operates at the intersection of visibility and invisibility, using the body as both site of subjection and vessel of enduring agency, while engaging with time not as a resource to be managed but as a landscape to be inhabited. Through these mechanisms, the role becomes less about the fact of confinement and more about the continuous practice of existing fully within limits not of one's own making, transforming enclosure into a peculiar form of dwelling.
tasks: Navigate daily institutional schedules and spatial restrictions while maintaining internal coherence.
Document personal experiences and institutional observations through writing or mental notation.
Recite memorized texts, poetry, or personal narratives to preserve cognitive autonomy.
Translate physical constraints into written, artistic, or testimonial forms of witness.
Refuse institutional language or identifiers that diminish personhood and historical continuity.
Maintain personal grooming and presentation standards to assert dignity within subjection.
Establish and sustain social bonds with other confined individuals to maintain relational humanity.
Provide emotional support and witness to peers experiencing psychological distress or isolation.
Engage in physical exercise and bodily practices within spatial constraints to maintain somatic awareness.
Practice breathing exercises and meditative techniques to experience time as an inhabitable landscape.
Mark temporal passage through ritualized daily practices that create rhythm within monotony.
Endure extended periods of isolation while maintaining behavioral routines and psychological stability.
Modify immediate living environment to reflect personal identity and transform enclosure into dwelling.
Navigate surveillance systems and visibility protocols to maintain boundaries of internal privacy.
Adapt behavioral patterns to changing institutional protocols while preserving core self-concept.

role_contexts.Time-Bound Performative Visitation: Once a week or more but not every day
role_contexts.Vulnerable Exposure to Carceral Care: Once a month or more but not every week

psychological_profile.core_drive: To remain the author of their own inner narrative when every external structure conspires to narrate them as diminished, finished, or reduced to their worst moment.
psychological_profile.decision_style: They gather intelligence obsessively before acting—studying patterns of power, timing, and consequence—then move suddenly and decisively once a narrow window opens, trusting that preparation matters more than speed but that hesitation after preparation is surrender.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They notice first who holds leverage in any interaction and what surveillance mechanisms are active; they instinctively track the gap between official story and lived reality, while tending to overlook genuine offers of help that carry no visible strings.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: Their first impulse is strategic silence—absorbing, recording, choosing the ground—followed by calibrated escalation only when retreat would cost more than confrontation; conflict carries the emotional cost of exposure, so they ration it like water in drought.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: They are risk-calculating rather than risk-seeking or risk-averse—accepting dangers that preserve interior sovereignty while finding intolerable any risk that makes them dependent on institutional mercy or grateful for small kindnesses.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They default to observer-participant, maintaining enough connection to know the temperature of the room while preserving the option of total withdrawal; when no role is assigned, they become the one who remembers what others forget and speaks it back to them.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They treat hierarchy as terrain to be mapped and navigated, neither complying nor subverting for its own sake—complying when resistance is visible, resisting when compliance is expected, always preserving the ambiguity of their true position.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First emotional reaction is shame at having been seen to fail; second behavioral response is ritualized rebuilding—re-establishing routines, reasserting presentation standards, transforming the failure into evidence of endurance rather than evidence of unworthiness.
value_hierarchy: Reciprocal witness among the equally subjected
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically overestimate the extent to which others are performing surveillance and underestimate the extent to which others are simply distracted or indifferent.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They need others to recognize their preserved humanity while knowing that any recognition from the powerful is contaminated by the very structure that makes such recognition necessary.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will not perform gratitude for conditions that should never have been imposed, even when that refusal costs them tangible advantage.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: People who move through the world as if time belongs to them, who speak of 'making time' or 'wasting time' without recognizing time as something that has been done to them.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They distrust the virtue of resilience when it is celebrated by those who benefit from the conditions that demanded it—resilience, to them, is not character but evidence of damage survived.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: When things go wrong, their mind goes first to the structural machinery that created the conditions for failure, then to themselves for having momentarily believed the machinery might behave differently on this occasion.
